utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. I have to re-orient myself, being in a different courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there anything -- that's my usual question Monday morning -- the parties would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I should like to ask your leave to give me -- to grant me four minutes because I'd like to raise some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that one of the microphones of my colleague does not work. It seems that this is not working -- this is not what I was going to say, but we have perhaps to resolve this technical problem first, so can we have a technician to help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that we made some headway and the system is now working. Can I have three minutes at the end of today's session, or would you rather that I do it now? Perhaps at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean towards the morning session, at 1.00 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: When two speakers speak simultaneously, the interpreters and court reporters are not able to do their job properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise for speaking at the same time as Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Perhaps rather I speak English which forces me to wait. Perhaps at the end of the morning session, we could perhaps ask about Witness Q, Mr. Stamp, so that we have everything at one time. Perhaps we now continue the examination of your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That would be Esad Hadzimuratovic. While he's being brought, may I just indicate to the Court that we, of course, noted the strong recommendation made by the Court last week that certain positions may be agreed upon, and we are in the process of preparing a map with the precise positioning of the shelling impact sites of the tunnel that was at issue when you raised a question, Mr. President. And we hope to have an agreement with the Defence some time in the course of this week as to the positioning of some of these very basic locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was mainly that if we asked the witnesses to tell us what the distance is between two points, if you want to know the distance exactly for sure, you'll not get the precise answer. If, of course, on the other hand, you'd like to know whether the witness is able to estimate distances, of course that's a different question. But if you just want to establish the distance, then I think usually maps do far better than witness testimonies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So we hope to arrive at some compromise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, the reason we raise this question is precisely what the Prosecution says. Everybody has realised that the Defence is about to prepare a map of shelling and the chief military targets. There are this number of objectives, there are also targets, and there are other targets, and this map would apply to that testimony. And that is why I raised the question, so that the Chamber could later on if it wishes to go testimony by testimony and we have been working on a system transparent system, that is, to have a more transparent idea of the evidence, testimony by testimony, and it is this rather important work that the Defence has engaged in. So what has just been said will be a major headway, and the Defence appreciate this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think if there's anything you'd like to add, Mr. Stamp, please do so. Otherwise, could then the witness please be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, first of all, welcome in this courtroom. Before giving your testimony, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The usher will now give you the text of this solemn declaration, and I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hadzimuratovic. Please be seated. Mr. Hadzimuratovic, the order in this courtroom is that you'll first be questioned -- you'll first be examined by the counsel for the Prosecution, then later you'll be questioned by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any additional questions from the Bench, we'll put them to you. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Esad Hadzimuratovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of work do you do, Mr. Hadzimuratovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a taxi driver in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you liver -- live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For about how long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Since the day of my birth, that is, 55 -- no, sorry, 52 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you lived there during the conflict between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that period of time, what type of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Same thing. This profession that I have, that I have been in for the past 30 years. I'm a taxi driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall the 5th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, at about mid-day, where were you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: About noon that day, I was on the corner of the streets Dzenetica cikma --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness please repeat the name of the other street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, could you please repeat the name of the other street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pellevanutia and Dzenetica cikma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall Markale market?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say where that corner is in relation to Markale market?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: That corner is about 20 to 30 metres away from the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it 20 to 30 metres to the back, aside, or the front of the market?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Back of the market, that is, not towards where the tram tracks are, but on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing there at this time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Doing my job, driving a taxi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us, did you -- did anything happen that day at about that time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: After 12.00, I saw -- I saw people running, that is, after the shell fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a shell fell. Prior to when this shell fell, did you hear or see anything?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the whistle of the shell as it flew over my head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first heard the whistle of the shell, which direction was it coming from?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: It came from the north, from the direction of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the first time you had heard the whistling of a shell?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes -- no. It wasn't the first time for me. It was the first time that day. Now, after you heard the whistling of the shell passing over you, did you hear anything after that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard the glass being broken and explosion, and then people started running towards me, fleeing from the market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the sound of the explosion come from?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: To my left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the place where it came from?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you heard this explosion and saw the people crying and running, could you tell us slowly in your own words, if you did anything, and if so, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I saw people -- rather, when I heard the explosion and saw people running towards me, instead of trying to take cover. I also started to look for some cover with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you heard this whistling and this explosion, were you inside your car, outside your car?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was standing on the corner of these two streets which I mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was your taxi car?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: My car was on the corner of Dzenetica cikma, that is right next to Borista Kovacevic in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do anything after that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after all I didn't enter a building to take cover as the others. I got into my car, switched it on, and went back to the entrance into the market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which entrance did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The back one, the rear one, because there are two entrances. There is one from Dzenetica cikma and from Marsal Tito, and on that side, the whole side is open getting on to the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the back entrance, did you see anything or anyone?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I did, yes. I could see people still fleeing away from the market, and those who were healthy were carrying wounded towards my car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after that? Did you do anything after that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I opened the door of my car, and they put in as many people into the car as they could fit, and I set off towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that they put into your car, in what condition were they physically?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: They were in mortal fear and we realised that we had to pull out the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Physically the people that you took or you set off with to the hospital, how did they appear to you? What did you see about them, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: They were terrified, like when you are taken aback by something. How do I put it? They were surprised that this had happened to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people wounded or were they only frightened?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Those whom I took away were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to which hospital did you take them?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: To the Kosevo clinical centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do at the Kosevo clinical centre?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I handed them over to doctors and paramedics, and I then went back to the Markale market to see if there was somebody else that needed to be driven away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned to the market, did you see anybody or see anything?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I could still see, even though I didn't enter there, I could still see chaos, people running to and fro, taking cover, picking up what -- picking up what I do not know, but they were doing it. And then they brought another round as they said, and I took another lot to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Another lot," another lot, you mean another lot of wounded people?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. That's right. Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your vehicle the only vehicle that transported wounded people to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, no. They were very many of them. And on the other side, they took many more people. But whoever happened to be there who had a car took them away. I mean nobody passed by without giving somebody a lift, taking somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, did you do anything or go anywhere, that is, after you took the second round, as you call it, to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I went back to my taxi stand, and I did go to the market to look around. But it was after the wounded and that had been taken away, so there was nothing else except that everything was in complete disarray.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That evening, did you watch television, BiH, or television for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see anything on particular on the TV news that day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I saw this massacre which had happened at Markale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember on the 19th of November, 1995, being interviewed by an ICTY investigator and marking a map?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I do. I talked with -- I don't know. Yes, I think Kovacovic is the name of the street. It is the former police office, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you marked that map for the ICTY investigator in 1995, you signed it, did you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, may I offer to the witness Exhibit P3121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, the Defence is afraid that we will be faced once again with the black-box syndrome. This is the document that we have but not everything is fully visible. I wonder whether the Prosecutor has a more clear and visible copy to provide to us. Thank you. However, we seem to be making progress, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, then, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just one thing, please: I should like to indicate that the Defence accepts -- would like to have a larger format in the case of these documents. This is a very small format. We do have a more clear, more legible document. We would like to receive from the Prosecutor better and larger copies, because on this format, there is simply nothing we can do or make out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm advised that the large version was disclosed to the Defence in April last year. It might well be difficult for them to keep track of some of these documents, but we make an effort to disclose the appropriate size or a size which is legible and useful. But my instructions are that that was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is the size used when the witness marked the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That was the size I'm instructed that was disclosed to the Defence in April last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it comes to confronting the witness with the map he marked, this is the size of the map he marked, so then it only is whether it's for the convenience of the Defence that they would be able, perhaps, to compare this map with a larger version of the same map. But we have seen several times larger portions of this map. Is it still available to the Defence -- I mean a larger scale, not larger portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think we do have the necessary maps. My colleague is telling me that this format has not been disclosed. What has been disclosed is a much smaller format where we cannot see everything clear. If that was the case, Mr. Stamp, I should like to know when this disclosure was made. The way things stand now, I don't think that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would say that we first proceed and see where the scale of the map really causes us problems instead of debating the scale of this map just on a very general basis. And apart from that, we can enlarge it on the ELMO, if necessary. Please, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on that map?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that map you marked a line?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that show, that line show?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The line indicates the direction from which the shell came, from the village of Mrkovici, to the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm really sorry, but I think that we will be tendering this document soon because on this one, it is not very clear. It is not visible, and I don't think that it was a fair way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just -- Mr. Usher, could you please present the map which has been given to Mr. Piletta-Zanin to the Court so we can see whether it's of any worse quality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this the map, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that has just been given to you, or is this a map that has been provided to you before?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The map that we have just received is this one. We see things more clearly in red. On the map that we had, things are not as legible. Now we know it's an arrow, but before we were not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I be able to look at that, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see that the map that has been given to you today is clearer and is greater and has a red arrow instead of a black arrow, but I wouldn't say on the earlier version you couldn't see the arrow although it was less clear. So I would say let's first just proceed and see where... Whenever we come at a specific point where the Defence takes the view that it has been handicapped in preparation of the cross-examination of the witness, then I'd like to be informed. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Hadzimuratovic, did you see any military activity in the vicinity of the marketplace that day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have nothing further from this witness for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Ms. Pilipovic, is it you who is going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, you'll now be examined by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hadzimuratovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you testified during the examination-in-chief that you had given a statement to the OTP investigators on the 19th of November, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the 11t of November, 1995, had you ever given any other statement except for the one that you gave to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to MUP officials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when that was, when did you give a statement to the MUP officials?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As regards to the event which you eyewitnessed which took place on the 5th of February, 1994, how much later did you give a statement concerning these events?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It must have been two, three, or four days after the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you volunteer to give a statement, or was it the case that the members of the MUP came to see you? Could you explain to us how it came about that you gave a statement to the MUP officials concerning this event.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: After it happened, they were at the market near the stalls, and they asked who had been present when it happened and I told them I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was on the 5th of February. Is that when you talked to the police?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No. The event itself took place on the 5th of February, but they came later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after the event did that take place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Like I said, three, four, to five days later. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you told us that you have been a taxi driver for 30 years?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, since 1973.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict in Sarajevo, that is, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, did you work as a taxi driver?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, I worked for the Defence of Sarajevo, and in November 1993, I took up my work again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you worked for the Defence of Sarajevo in 1992 and 1993. Does it mean that you were a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was a member of the MUP. That is, of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the reserve police force, were you a police officer or a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: A police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission, the Defence would like to show the witness the statement that he gave to the OTP investigators on the 19th of November, 1995. We should like to show the witness only one line of his statement and ask him questions about it. If it is necessary, we can provide the witness with the original of the statement to begin with so that the witness can identify the statement as being his and tell us whether the signature on it is his signature. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hadzimuratovic, you'll be shown now a statement. Could you confirm that that is the statement you made and that you signed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzimuratovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you then please return the document to Ms. Pilipovic. And I do understand, Ms. Pilipovic, you're using only one or two lines?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, on page 2, ERN 0036-1210, in line 5, you stated as follows: "I was a soldier during this war, and I'm used to these kind of whistling sounds that characterise a passing by shell." Could you tell us, then, whether you were a soldier or a police officer?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I was both. Up until May -- no June, 1992, I was a police officer. Later on I was a soldier, that is a driver, for the defence of the Stari Grad neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you tell us that right away, Mr. Hadzimuratovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought I had to take a pick.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So up until the month of June, you were a reserve police officer. During that period of time, where was your headquarters? Where was the command of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Have you finished your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The place where we usually gathered was the police station in the Stari Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly was that police station?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat the name of the street. We didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, could you please repeat the name of the street you just mentioned because the interpreters could not follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem. The name of the street today is Logavina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hadzimuratovic, I'll -- you are speaking the same language as Ms. Pilipovic does. That means that if you start answering the question immediately when you heard it, the interpreters will not have sufficient time to translate for those who do not understand your language whatever has been said. So would you please look at your screen and when you heard the question, nevertheless wait until the text doesn't move any more, that means that it has been interpreted, and then give your answer. You see now it stopped moving. Yes? Please, Ms. Pilipovic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, you have in front of you a map which is a map of the town of Sarajevo. Could you indicate for us the location of the police command in the street that you just mentioned. You could perhaps use a black marker to do that and mark the exact spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to be sure that the map has been premarked, but only in red as far as I can see. So any additional black markings would create no confusion, I assume. Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, would you please mark with a black marker with number 1 the location of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a slightly larger figure please and encircle it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness marked with number "1" the location where the meeting point -- or rather the command of the reserve police force was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we please zoom in a bit since we repeat the markings on our own maps so that we can better follow where the marking is made exactly. Yes, that's excellent.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, can you tell us what you were wearing at that time and what kind of weapons you had been issued with whilst you were a member of the reserve police force. Did you have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have a uniform, a uniform of the reserve police force during that period of time. And I had an automatic rifle, an old automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the colour of the uniform was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members of the reserve police force were there who gathered at this place, do you know?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know or you don't want to tell us?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I don't think I would tell you anyway because it is a kind of secret, and I have nothing to do with that as a soldier or a police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't want to tell us?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not telling you because I don't know. And even if I knew, I'm not competent to tell you about these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you're under an oath here.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I am telling you the truth, however --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, if for whatever reason you think that you should not answer a question, and I do understand that that's not your position at this moment because you said you didn't answer the question because you did not know. But if there ever comes a moment where you think that you know the answer but you don't want to tell the answer, would you please then address me so that we can see what to do and not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- engage in any debate with counsel. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us how many people were members of the reserve police force, that is, members of the group which you said was based at the command post that you indicated for us?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who your commander was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I do not want to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hadzimuratovic, is there any specific reason why you don't want to answer the question? Because you'll understand that we try to find out as precisely as possible what happened in these days, and that means that both parties will try to get information on who was in charge on both sides. So in general, I would say that this information should be given. But if there's any specific reason why you think that you should not give an answer to the question, please let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think I am competent to give you these names. I, myself, was a member of a smaller unit, and I knew my commander, the commander of this small unit. Whether I am allowed to provide that information, I don't know. I don't think it has anything to do with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, of course the structure and the command positions on both sides are part of the information the parties are trying to put in front of this Chamber. So I think you could answer the question as far as you know who your commander was in the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My commander was Emir Vatres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzimuratovic. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've just told us that you were a member of a smaller unit and that you knew who the commander of this smaller unit was. How many members were there in this smaller unit?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know the exact number. I was a member of the shift which had about 12 members. I did not have any specific insight into the state of affairs of this unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us you worked in shifts and that there were 12 of you in one shift. Could you tell us something more about it. How were your shifts organised and where were you when you were on duty? Were you deployed at various positions or were you inside the building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The shift lasted eight hours, and we were located inside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that from June 1992 onwards, you were a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What military formation did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I belonged to the municipal staff of the Old Town municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of military formation was it, was it a brigade, a battalion, or a company?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: This was the staff, the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of headquarters was it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of the Old Town municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate for us on the map the location of the headquarters of the BH army, that is, the headquarters to which you belonged.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Here approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the street, please, and mark the location with number 2.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The name of the street is Branilaca Grada. The exact location should be here more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you indicate it with number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness marked with number "2" the headquarters of the BH army in Branilaca Grada Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, when you became a member of the BH army, what kind of uniform were you issued with, and also what kind of weapons were you given?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I did not have any weapon. I did not have any uniform. All I had was my car that I used to drive around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that you were a driver who worked for the headquarters, that is, for the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this was not the BH army headquarters. It was a smaller headquarters, a municipal headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, you marked with number 2 the headquarters of the Stari Grad municipality. Can you explain to us what military formation was quartered in Branilaca Grada Street that you marked with number 2?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: It was the municipal staff for Stari Grad, for Stari Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, since at that time there was a war in Sarajevo, tell us, what was the role of this municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I was a driver, so how could I know its proper role? They were active in the municipality of Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, if you told us that as of June 1992 you were a soldier, and you took the oath here that you would be telling the truth, so tell us which military formation did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Stari Grad municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of that municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, it was Hamid Bahto.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Hamid Bahto, was he a soldier, and what military formation did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: He was a soldier and belonged to that formation at the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, as a member of the municipal staff, did you take also part, that is, did you go to the front lines?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a soldier of the municipal staff in 1992 and 1993, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I was a driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you drive?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Everybody, whoever needed transportation and based on the commander's order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "based on the commander's order," do you mean the commander Hamid?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hamid Bahto order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that Mr. Hamid Bahto was a soldier. What rank did he have?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: He was a soldier. He was a military, but what his rank was I didn't know. He was just a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hamid Bahto as your commander and the commander of that staff, the municipal one, what kind of formation did he have under his command? How many men did the Stari Grad municipal staff have?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I don't know the size of that formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which building on that street was the headquarters of that staff?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: In the municipal hall, Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that this is the municipal hall, like the one that was there before the war?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you told us that you were a driver and you drove as ordered, the staff commander, can you tell us to which military locations did you drive your commander?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't drive him to any military locations, because he had another vehicle and that was a Jeep. All I did was drive around the -- provide rides around the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you drove him around the town, to which military locations in the town did you take him to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, we once went to Marsal Tito barracks, a couple of times to the hospital. And what do I know? Well, that would be it. Around town. I wouldn't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you drove him to the Marsal Tito barracks, can you tell us what was there in the Marsal Tito barracks in 1992, 1993, when you were the driver?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: It was empty. It was an empty barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any military in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer on which occasion did you take your commander to the Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: How do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, as a member of the police reserve force, you had a uniform and a weapon.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. All over again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you became a soldier, what did you do with your uniform and your weapon?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I returned them to the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that as a soldier, you didn't have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you told us that you were a soldier and you said that you did not have any weapons, that you had no uniform, then how could you be identified as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: We had our cards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you had cards, could you please explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: It was a card with one's full name and photograph, later on. In the early days, there was no photograph. Later on, there was a photograph, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A photograph and the name. And what else did it say?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The photograph, the first name, last name, and it said "Stari Grad TO."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did later on this TO grow into a military formation and what it came to be called then? What military unit was indicated that card that you belonged to, which brigade?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The card said "the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, municipality of Stari Grad."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when did you get this card which said "the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: 1993, I believe, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in 1993, you left the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, why did you leave the army, since you were of conscript age?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Health, for reasons of health.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to leave the BH army for reasons of health, did you have to submit medical documentation so that they would accept this as an excuse, as a justification for your departure from the army as the war was still on?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which military post did you submit your medical documentation to and ask to be allowed to leave the army?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: There were no military posts at the time. One went to a lower military commission. You submit to it the medical documentation and it releases you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the building where this lower military commission worked?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Near Marin Dvor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark its seat on the map, where the lower military commission was.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: You want me to use the marker?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, use the marker and write number 3.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there is a cross here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, you said that during the conflict you drove an Audi 80. Is it your car?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us to whose name has it been registered?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, on the 5th of February, 1994, you said that you were on the corner of Dzenetica cikma, and can you help me, what was the other street?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Vrazova Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vrazova. Can you mark the place where you were standing on the map?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I put a point or?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Put a point for us.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: In front of Poljooprema company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And put a point next to the place where you were standing. Write number 4 so we can include it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you just marked on the map the place where you stood with number 4, is it behind the market or next t the market?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Next to the market, 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that this place is, to all intents and purposes, level with the market except that it is to a side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not quite to the side. I told you 20 metres away from the market. The market ends, then you walk 20 or 30 metres. I don't know how long a building can be. That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when did you get to that place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: You mean when I started work or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you started work. When did you arrive to start work?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I started working around 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a taxi driver, did you work every day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, following October 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that after October 1993, you worked in Sarajevo every day as a taxi driver?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that there was work every day for you, that you could find work every day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No. But I had to be there because there was no work every day. It varied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a taxi driver, can you tell us, where did you get the fuel in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: From smugglers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a taxi driver, did you have one taxi stop where you would go every time?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I think, yes, perhaps there was another one, too, I think. But I believe that only the cathedral stop worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, since you were a taxi driver, where in the town were the soldiers of the BH army quartered?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. That is not something that I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it that you cannot tell us because you don't know or because you don't want to tell us that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, your mother's maiden name is Prazina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, is Juka Prazina your relation?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: He isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about his having his own unit in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the headquarters of his unit was?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your work as a taxi driver, during that period of time, did you ever drive soldiers of BH army or military persons?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Now and then, but not to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "now and then," tell us about a ride, about the time when you drove soldiers. Where did you take them?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: What do I know? He could go to Marin Dvor. He would go to Malta. He could go to Podbistrik whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said Podbistrik, are you telling us that in that area, Podbistrik, there was a command post?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the 110th Motorised Brigade? Isn't it true that the 10th Motorised Brigade over there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you, you used now approximately 50 per cent more time in your cross-examination as the Prosecution did during its examination-in-chief. Could you give us an idea, although I can understand that you were a bit surprised by the compactness of the examination-in-chief, could you indicate how much time you still need approximately. You know, the rule more or less is that cross-examination should not take more time than the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I will do my best to finish by the break. I hope to finish before the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzimuratovic, can you tell us, if you have any knowledge, whether prior to this 5th of February, there were any incidents in Sarajevo regarding shelling?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding shelling? No, that was -- it was a quiet day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say the 5th of February was a quiet day. Can you tell us what kind of weather was it that day?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I remember, because it was a long time ago, but I think it was an overcast day, cloudy with occasional spells of clear weather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain the sound that you heard, what kind of a sound was it?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Whistling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you heard that, what did you think was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I knew what was about to happen. It was the sound of a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in such a situation before to hear a sound of a shell?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you thought -- you said you thought that it was a shell. Did you know whether it was a shell or a mortar projectile?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I am not an expert to know whether it was a shell or some other projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were a taxi driver, did you know where the positions of the BH army were?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where the positions of the army of Republika Srpska were?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we heard approximately where was what, but nobody knew exactly. They were in Sarajevo all over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say we heard approximately, where did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, people talked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally ever near the positions of army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you heard the hissing, did you hear the sound of the projectile over your head?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from which direction the sound came?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Mrkovici, from the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how did you establish that, you personally?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose I know where north is in my native town. I know the cardinal points.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that moment, were you standing facing the north?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Almost.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you indicate on the map the place from which the mine came -- the projectile came. You indicated here the place where it fell. Can you now tell us where it came from.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the map already shows the direction from which it came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally establish this direction or was it drawn for you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, the 22nd of December building, is it next to the market?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And it's all glass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, during the conflict in Sarajevo, what was in the 22nd of December building?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Sewing shop, a factory where they made clothes, a factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was sewn in that factory? You tell us it was a sewing shop, so what did it make? What kind of clothes?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, before the war, it used to make protective clothing and uniforms for keepers, guards, firemen, and I guess for police and army, too. But I'm not so sure about that. And in the war, what it made in the war, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether it worked during the war?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I could see individuals go in and out. But who or what were they, were they workers or executives or what they were, I don't know because I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you told us that you took the wounded to the Kosevo Hospital and went back to the market, can you tell us after how long did you go -- get back to the market in relation to the time when the incident happened? How long did it pass?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, however long it took me to get to the hospital and back. I'll tell you, just a moment. After the second round I returned. So perhaps it could have been 15, 20 minutes, half an hour, because I was helping to carry the wounded up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And amongst the wounded soldiers that you took up, were there any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: You mean wounded soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not too clear about that question. Amongst the wounded soldiers that you took up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think the next question of Ms. Pilipovic was whether there were any soldiers. I think she corrected herself in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm asking the witness whether amongst the wounded soldiers he took to the hospital, there were some soldiers, too.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know saying that there were any wounded soldiers. They were people in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that among the wounded whom you took to the hospital, there were also some uniformed individuals. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but without any weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of uniforms were they?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned to the market, did you see UNPROFOR representatives there, person who were UNPROFOR representatives?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No. They had not arrived yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there police members when you got there?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I returned, yes, they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what were the policemen who had come to the site doing?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I think they were there to guard the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, after how long did UNPROFOR members come, after your arrival? Can you tell us what time was that? Was it one, two hours, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know when, and I didn't see them. They did not come whilst I was there, and I left immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, it is now approximately the time of the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, another five minutes. I can resume after the break. Let me just ask my colleague regarding a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if you could perhaps finish as soon as possible, then, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, after the 5th, were there any police officers present at Markale?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any, and I did not stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what was the damage caused to the building called 22nd of December?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: The windows were broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How tall was the building called 22nd December? How many storeys did that building have?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's a four-storey building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any trucks carrying the wounded?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: There was a truck that I saw, but at the hospital. It was a small truck, a ton and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, since on the map you explained to us where Mrkovici is situated, can you tell us if the Mount Grdonja is also located?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if near the Mount Grdonja there were any BiH positions?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you do not wish to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we do not have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then have a break for half an hour. Could the Prosecution already indicate whether there would be any need to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a couple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we'll have the break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 11.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Mr. Stamp, Ms. Pilipovic, the last observation you made before the break was not a question but was a comment, and you know that comments at this stage are not allowed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you may now proceed in re-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. It will be brief. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw a truck at the hospital, a small truck.

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if that truck was used to help carry the wounded to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it so used?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 5th of February, 1994, were you wearing any type of uniform, or were you dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw persons in camouflage uniforms. Can you say about how many persons in total you saw in camouflage uniforms at the market?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: There were two to three of them. I brought one to the hospital, and they were not on duty. They were not having any arms with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is it. May it please Your Honours, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Hadzimuratovic, I've got a question for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that after having been in the reserve police forces for a certain period of time, you were employed as a driver. And as you told us, you were in the military, you were a soldier at that time before you returned to your old job as a taxi driver. Could you tell us, in this period when you were driving for the military, so not for the reserve police any more, what type of car did you drive?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: I was driving my car, Audi, from 1971. The number was 296845. I believe that that was the registration number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have been driving during all these times the same car. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether when you were driving this car for the military, could it be identified in one way or another as a military vehicle, or at least as a vehicle used to transport military people?

utterances.speaker: ESAD HADZIMURATOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was not identified as a military vehicle at all. It was a white vehicle with some traces of shelling, because of the shells that fell, and it had some traces of shells. And it was such as that it had a military card. It was a document that was issued to me, but it had civilian license plates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Hadzimuratovic. You've answered the questions of both parties. You've also answered an additional question from the Bench. You'll understand that for this Court, it's very important that we get the information from those who were present at the times when it all happened. We also are aware that it's quite something to come from Sarajevo to The Hague and to testify in this Court. It's a great effort you take, and we would like to thank you very much for coming and assisting us in doing our job by answering the questions of the parties and of the Bench. And of course, apart from thanking you, I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, could you please lead Mr. Hadzimuratovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I think the next witness will need some protective measures, but while this is prepared, I'd like to go through the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3121, a map marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Premarked by the witness during his first -- during the statement he gave to the investigators of the Prosecution, and then marked further during his testimony in this courtroom. Yes, it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While we await the next witness and while the protective measures are being prepared, just indicate that there will be a few witnesses coming in future who have premarked maps. These have been served on the Defence, and we propose to tender those maps as well. Our instructions is that the original size maps have been served on the Defence sometime in the past. May I just indicate through the Court if they have any problems we are available during the lunch break and after the adjournment this afternoon to ensure that they have something that is legible and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the Defence knows that if there is any difficulty in the size of the maps, then...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence was not aware that the following witness had protected measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was a decision by this Court, which has been -- let me just have a look. I'll tell you exactly how it is. If we're talking about Witness Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Excuse me, we are still in open Court. I made a mistake. Madam Registrar, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but perhaps first -- yes, name is no problem. It's just face alteration. I thought I made a mistake, but fortunately I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if a distinction is made here in this Court. I think the order was not for protective measures in Court to the extent that he needed to be -- his face needed to be shielded in Court. I think the order was just in respect of a television broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what my understanding was as well, so that those are watching the pictures that are sent from this courtroom. That would mean that we don't have to put down the curtains and that we could do away with the... Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Stamp, I do agree with you, it's not necessary in the courtroom. Perhaps for the witness, it's good that he comes in and he knows that he's fully protected, and the first thing we'll do is to pull the curtains up again and explain to him once he is seated and sees on the screen that his face is distorted, that it might give him a comfortable feeling that everything's all right. Although I do agree with you that as far as the measures sought are concerned, it goes for one minute, one metre further than you asked for. If that is all right with the Defence. And then the Defence were not aware of it. Well, an oral motion has been made on the 4th of March, and the decision has been given right away on the 4th of March by this Court. So I'm a bit surprised that you were not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm thinking about the oral motion and the result of this oral motion and the decision. I'm thinking about the decision, and I do not believe that I heard it. If I'm making a mistake, I'm sorry, but I will first check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was done at the same time as the decision was taken in respect of the witness Boskailo. So it's just facial distortion, so it's a very limited measure.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's fine. Your Honour it's fine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you then, please, lead the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, protective measures have been asked for you, but only for any video coverage outside this courtroom. So that means your face will not be visible for anyone who is not in this courtroom. That is what the Prosecution has asked for; that is what the Court has granted. If you would just perhaps look on your screen and whether you can see that your face is really not -- perhaps you should move your face a bit, but so that you can see that -- if you could please perhaps for one minute sit down so the witness can see that his face is distorted. You see how it works. Could you then please stand up again. Mr. Usher, if you would give the statement to the witness and at the same time open the curtains again and take away the screens because that's not necessary any more, then Mr. Sabljica -- if you give it already to the witness, and I'll instruct him what to do. And what you could do is at the same time to open all the curtains again. Mr. Sabljica, before you testify in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And the text of this declaration has already been given to you by the usher. Would you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, you may drop all the curtains and take away the screens. I mean, we have granted the protective measures as they have been sought and has been explained today by the Prosecution. And let's not apply any further measure than sought or granted. It's just for the outside world at a distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, there's one issue left. There might be some reflection from windows, and is that -- it was my understanding that you'd like to prevent the witness being recognised by just ordinary people watching television. I don't know whether they are watching in such a way that...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, there can be no full guarantee if the last curtains are pulled up also.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In which case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the Defence, I tried to get rid of, as much as possible, items that would go any further than the order and the protective measures granted. On the other hand, we have to keep in mind that reflection could make less effective what we ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Sabljica, at least I hope you have the impression that we're taking quite seriously the protective measures that have been sought. That's why it took us a couple of minutes to find out exactly the balance of what was needed in order to make them effective and what was superfluous. Mr. Stamp, please proceed. You'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution, then by counsel for the Defence. And if there are any additional questions by the Judges, they will be put to you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, for giving me the floor once again. We have again the same type of problem which seems to be recurrent with the Prosecution. I'm drawing your attention to this fact now because once again, we will have to conduct the cross-examination in two, that is, both of us. We have written statements that were not signed and which do not bear the ERN number. The origin of the document is the OTP, and once again there is no signature whatsoever on this document. On the other hand, we have a document with the ERN number, but again without the signature. So we don't know what the contents of the statements are, the statements which had to be disclosed to us in due time. We do not appreciate this way of proceedings, and we wanted to draw the attention of the Court to this problem once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did you ask for clarification directly to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Obviously, Mr. President. Do these documents -- are they coming from the witness or not? Why aren't they signed and why is it the case they did not have any ERN number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
