utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the OTP. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yes. Since the question has been answered, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at that document. Is that the original of the copy which you looked at earlier?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Item 3 in the legend, and as marked in the map, is what? Could you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: A market stall. And this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Item 5 in the legend, you described to be the 22nd of December building. Could you tell the Court the height of the building which you recorded.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: 18.450 millimetres, or if you like, 18 metres 450 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if this would be a convenient time. I was just about to move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's a convenient time to conclude for this moment at least the examination of the witness. On the other hand, I wonder which of the documents are you going to tender? The original one, well legible, or are you preparing another well legible copy, or what can we expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would be very grateful, since you suggested it, Mr. President, if we could be allowed to obtain a better copy of the original. We do tend to keep the originals as secure as possible for any type of references for example of this nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well since all the parties have had an opportunity to check specifically on those aspects which are badly legible, we'll decide on it tomorrow. So you'll have an opportunity to come up with a better copy. Then I would say that we have three minutes left. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you asked for three minutes. I'd like to give them to you at this very moment, but perhaps first to ask the usher to lead the witness out of the courtroom, but not until I've checked with the technical booth that while leaving the courtroom -- no, it's not necessary to pull the curtains down, Mr. Usher. Can I get a confirmation from the technical booth that the witness will not be on the video while leaving the courtroom. Yes, Mr. Usher, you may lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not mine, but I believe there are people in the public gallery, and I believe that they should be noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well first of all the Prosecution has told us that the protective measures do not relate to those who are in the public gallery. And it's mainly before -- for the outgoing video picture and I secured that he will not appear on that. So Mr. Usher, would you please lead Mr. Sabljica out of the courtroom. And tomorrow morning, we'll resume at 9.00 but in a different courtroom, Mr. Sabljica. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, thank you, Your Honour, for giving me the floor. I shall be very brief. The reason we have to stand up is because we now need more than ever help and consideration of your Chamber. We are now examining one of the most important elements of this indictment, and that is some of the shellings which happened in the Markale market. And we are now for the up to the time asking for certain exhibits so that we could prepare our cross-examination. We believe that there are two series of documents. However, since so far we have not received any information at all from the Prosecution, I think we shall have to keep asking where that is all the time, now, and again. But we would much rather that your Chamber invite us specifically, concretely, the Prosecution to let us know as soon as possible when it comes to our examination of this expert witness, one, what we know and do not know the set of some 72 pieces of this shrapnel of the fragments which were photographed, where are they? Where are these pieces? Have they been located? When will they be brought to The Hague? This is the first time matter. And secondly, we would directly like to know the orders and maps of the main staff which are related to it and which is also important when we talk about the staff operation the I have repeated asked for it, and we have not yet received any answer except not legible and there is another matter. And I shall be very brief, Mr. President, and which is after all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. my custom, and that is the production of exhibits. You see that we have all difficulties here because we are receiving some copies which are simply not legible. With we see the originals, we see that they are quite legible. So I do not know why we cannot be given clearer copies because everybody would save time. And on the same -- in the same vein, last week, time was lost by many people because some tapes were produced bearing certain numbers. What I needed to say here is that since we were talking about two tapes which were tendered by the Prosecution and which have 2279 and 2279A, at that time we did not receive under the normal procedure these tapes with their correct numbers, and that is why we had to go back to our place to go through all this material, and we simply could not check the correctness of the first tape without the one which was tendered under a different number to your Chamber. Therefore, could you come up with a ruling, please, under which the Prosecution, whenever it places a number on its exhibit, gives us this exhibit, a copy of it under the correct number. That would facilitate matters greatly. And then we shall be saving time in the future. Thank you very much, Mr. President, in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you've heard what Mr. Piletta-Zanin said. I think the Chamber will consider before tomorrow whether we'll go back into the tape history again. I see that Mr. Piletta-Zanin does not insist on going back into the tape history. But there was a commitment of the Prosecution of last week about the photographs, pieces of shrapnel, and orders and maps, to find out and inform the Chamber by the end of the week what could be found and what their position was. I do not remember that we have an answer yet. Are you able to give it right away, or would this be the first thing you'd like to do tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We would do it the first thing tomorrow morning because we have quite a few ancillary issues to do tomorrow morning. And I could be a very precise if we deal were it then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll wait until tomorrow morning. Perhaps I may have made a small mistake to the extent that I might have made a small mistake to the extent that I indicated to the witness that we will resume tomorrow at 9.00. On the other hand, we also indicated to the parties before to the parties that we'll deal with the 92 bis issue to start with tomorrow morning. So perhaps a message could be sent to the Victims and Witness Unit that the presence of the witness is not necessary right away at 9.00, it will take us certainly at least half an hour -- I hope less -- but it will certainly take us approximately half an hour to deal with some of the issues. Is there anything else at this moment? Then we'll adjourn until 9.00 tomorrow morning in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 12th day of March, 2000, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
